covers.title: Rapid quenching by ram-pressure stripping in a young cluster at $z = 1.7$

assertions.text: We believe this is a result for Nature rather than a specialist venue because it bears on the general question of how environment and stellar mass divide the quenching budget, and because the measurement is reproducible end to end: every panel in the paper is generated by a script archived beside it.

The advance is a directly measured stripping radius, molecular reservoir and kinematic asymmetry in the same object at $z > 1$ — the regime in which the quenched populations these clusters now contain were assembled, and in which every previous constraint has been statistical.
No related manuscript by any author is under consideration or in press elsewhere.

abbreviatedSummary: A galaxy caught mid-stripping in a z = 1.7 cluster loses its star-forming gas from the outside in, on a timescale short enough to explain the quenched population these clusters already contain.
